intent.outcome: Every authoritative plan-resource mutation serializes through PlanWriteTxn; multi-file operations stage, validate, and commit via a recovery manifest so concurrent CLI processes cannot allocate duplicate IDs or leave partially committed promotions/archives.

problem.description: Most backlog/track/annotation/brief/session/idea writers bypass with_plan_write_lock. Multi-file promotions and archive flows write one resource then another with only per-file atomicity, so crashes and races produce lost updates, duplicate IDs, and inconsistent source/target metadata.

in_scope: PlanWriteTxn acquired by each authoritative plan-resource mutation
Route backlog, idea, brief, annotation, decision, track, session, specs, plan/config, migration, and archive mutations through the txn
Multi-file stage/validate/commit with versioned recovery manifest and idempotent promotion retries
Project-root lock for init/relocate; separate short-lived locks/CAS for Watch and agent runtime state
Post-commit best-effort activity append without re-acquiring the plan lock
out_of_scope: Lifecycle transition table and Raul UI fixes (Groups C–E)
Schema/input hardening and security trust boundaries (Groups B/F)
Comment cleanup and app.rs decomposition (Group G)
Holding the global plan lock for an entire Watch run lifetime

acceptance_criteria.description: Concurrent backlog add, track add, annotation create, brief update, and session mutation against one plan preserve unique IDs and both writers survive; a held plan write lock times out with a clear error and leaves source files byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Stage-10 re-review after F-08: isolated FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1/2 + success retry converge path+config; plan_relocate_failpoint covers 1+2; focused suites 26 passed; open findings 0; verify AC-01/02/03 ok

acceptance_criteria.description: Multi-file promotions, archive/restore, brief done/reopen, and session archive/promote either commit all staged resources or recover to one consistent plan state; retry after injected failure never creates a duplicate target; archive metadata always agrees with source status.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Stage-10 re-review after F-08: isolated FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1/2 + success retry converge path+config; plan_relocate_failpoint covers 1+2; focused suites 26 passed; open findings 0; verify AC-01/02/03 ok

acceptance_criteria.description: mp crate with tests compiles under Clippy with warnings denied after the PlanWriteTxn and transaction changes.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Stage-10 re-review after F-08: isolated FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1/2 + success retry converge path+config; plan_relocate_failpoint covers 1+2; focused suites 26 passed; open findings 0; verify AC-01/02/03 ok

design_decisions.choice: Authoritative plan-resource mutations acquire PlanWriteTxn; Watch and agent runtime state use separate short-lived locks or CAS and never hold the global plan lock for a Watch run lifetime.
design_decisions.rationale: A single flock convention was caller-optional and missed most collection writers; Watch must not self-deadlock against activity append or serialize the whole agent run.

design_decisions.choice: Multi-file ops compute all documents in memory, validate, stage, fsync, and commit via a versioned recovery manifest; activity append is best-effort after durable commit on a non-relocking path.
design_decisions.rationale: Per-file atomic_write cannot express promotion/archive consistency; nested flock on activity under an outer plan lock deadlocks.

design_decisions.choice: Promotion results carry source provenance so retries detect an existing target instead of allocating a duplicate.
design_decisions.rationale: Crash between target create and source resolve currently leaves both a new milestone/track item and an unresolved backlog/idea.

work_packages.name: PlanWriteTxn lock discipline
work_packages.goal: All authoritative plan-resource RMW paths acquire PlanWriteTxn; Watch/runtime stay on separate sync.

work_packages.name: Multi-file transaction engine
work_packages.goal: Stage/validate/commit with recovery manifest; idempotent promotions; activity post-commit non-relocking.

steps.action: Introduce PlanWriteTxn (or equivalent token) that acquires the plan/project-root write lock; make unlocked store helpers crate-private and callable only through the token; document nested-lock prohibition for activity.
steps.done_when: Txn API compiles; unit/integration lock tests still pass; activity has non-relocking append path under an outer txn.

steps.action: Route unlocked collection RMW writers through PlanWriteTxn: backlog, idea, brief, annotation, decision, track, session focus/config, specs init, plan metadata, and config set.
steps.done_when: Parallel backlog/track/annotation/brief/session writers allocate unique IDs and both survive; lock timeout leaves files byte-identical.

steps.action: Use project-root lock for init and plan relocate; keep Watch and agent runtime state on separate short-lived locks or CAS generations (never PlanWriteTxn for Watch lifetime).
steps.done_when: Relocate/init do not rely solely on a lock file inside a moving plan dir; Watch state updates do not hold the global plan lock for the run lifetime.

steps.action: Implement multi-file mutation module: load sources, compute results in memory, validate, stage, fsync, commit via versioned recovery manifest with rollback/recovery; manifests use bounded relative paths only.
steps.done_when: Failpoint suite exists; failure before each stage/rename yields no change or deterministic recovery.

steps.action: Migrate multi-file command flows onto the transaction module with source provenance for idempotent retries: backlog/idea/track promote, brief done/reopen/promote, track cancel/archive, session archive/promote, milestone archive/restore/purge, review pass where milestone+reviews both write.
steps.done_when: Injected mid-op failure never leaves source/target disagreeing; retry does not duplicate targets; archive metadata matches source status.

steps.action: Wire activity append as post-commit best-effort via txn non-relocking path; ensure execution/session/watch callers cannot re-acquire flock under an outer txn.
steps.done_when: No self-deadlock on activity under plan txn; journal failures warn without rolling back durable plan commits.

verification.evidence: Stage-10 re-review after F-08: isolated FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1/2 + success retry converge path+config; plan_relocate_failpoint covers 1+2; focused suites 26 passed; open findings 0; verify AC-01/02/03 ok

findings.description: PlanWriteTxn::run_recoverable rolled back intentional ExitCode exits (e.g. milestone bulk partial failure exit 2), undoing successful per-id writes. Fix: commit recovery when Err is ExitCode; only unexpected errors roll back.

Live multi-file edit and plan-path renames (archive/relocate) initially bypassed recoverable PlanWriteTxn / rename_plan_path failpoints. Remediatied by routing edit through recoverable txn and renaming via store::rename_plan_path with archive failpoint coverage.
findings.summary: Edit/rename must use recoverable txn paths

findings.description: Legacy promote tests expected hard rejection on re-promote after success; M187 idempotent-retry contract requires success with idempotent:true. Updated p9/p10 suite tests accordingly.
findings.summary: Align promote tests with idempotent retries

findings.description:
RecoveryTxn treats any surviving .mp-txn directory as incomplete and always restores the before-image on the next PlanWriteTxn::acquire (mutation_txn.rs recover_pending / restore_before_image; plan_io.rs run_recoverable commit only deletes the txn dir after op Ok). There is no durable commit marker, so a process kill after all authoritative writes succeed but before commit() removes .mp-txn leaves the new state on disk with a pending marker. The next unrelated writer silently rolls the completed mutation back.

Reproducer (debug mp):
  init; backlog add; MP_MUTATION_CRASH_AFTER_WRITE=2 mp backlog promote B-01 --to-track bugfix
  → on-disk: B-01 resolved, track has 1 item, .mp-txn pending
  → mp backlog add (any writer) recovers
  → B-01 active again, track items=0 (durable promotion undone)

AC-02 requires commit-all or recover to one consistent intended state; undoing a fully written mutation on an unrelated command is incorrect. Tests only inject mid-mutation crashes (fail_after 1/2 during writes), not post-success/pre-commit-cleanup.
findings.summary: Commit crash window undoes durable multi-file mutations

findings.description:
mp plan relocate uses PlanWriteTxn::acquire_project_root + txn.run (commands/plan.rs), not run_recoverable, despite being a multi-resource mutation in the Group A inventory. rename_plan_path is called first; on error after a durable rename there is no rollback (rollback only runs if write_config fails later).

Reproducer:
  MP_MUTATION_FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1 mp plan relocate master-plan relocated-plan
  → exit 1; master-plan gone; relocated-plan present; config workflow.plan.location still master-plan
  → subsequent mp commands cannot find the plan at the configured path

This is a torn multi-file commit outside the recovery manifest path M187 was meant to close.
findings.summary: plan relocate tears plan path vs config on rename failure

findings.description:
AC-02 requires archive metadata and source status to agree. TrackCmd::Purge routes to commands/archive.rs cmd_purge which calls store::purge_archived_milestone (file delete only). The milestone path correctly does remove_archive_meta_entry then purge (milestone/io.rs), but the track purge entry point skips meta removal.

Reproducer:
  milestone archive <id>; mp track purge archived milestone <id> --confirm
  → archive/milestones empty; archive/meta.json still lists the milestone entry

M187 inventory explicitly included track purge as a multi-resource op to migrate onto transactional consistency.
findings.summary: track purge deletes archive file but leaves meta entry

findings.description:
commands/archive.rs cmd_restore for track-item sets status=pending and clears archived_at on the track file but never calls remove_archive_meta_entry. After a successful restore, archive/meta.json still lists the track-item as archived while the source item is pending — AC-02 archive metadata disagreement.

Reproducer:
  track archive track-item bugfix BF-01; track restore archived track-item BF-01 --kind bugfix
  → item status pending; meta.entries still contains entity_id BF-01

Milestone restore correctly removes meta; track-item restore does not. Covered by M187 archive consistency scope / AC-02.
findings.summary: track-item restore leaves stale archive meta entry

findings.description:
F-05 remediation only rolls back rename_plan_path when the post-rename failpoint fires (FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1). Relocate still does rename then write_config under PlanWriteTxn::run (not run_recoverable). atomic_write persists config.json before mutation_write_failpoint; on FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=2 the config write fails after the location field is already durable, and commands/plan.rs rolls the directory back to the old path while leaving workflow.plan.location set to the new path inside that directory.

Reproducer (isolated temp project, release mp):
  mp init --force
  MP_MUTATION_FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=2 mp plan relocate master-plan relocated-plan
  → exit 1; master-plan present; relocated-plan absent; config workflow.plan.location == "relocated-plan"
  → subsequent mp commands look for the plan at the wrong path

FAIL_AFTER_WRITE=1 remains consistent (path+config both master-plan). Suite test plan_relocate_failpoint_rolls_back_path_and_config only covers fail_after=1 (L1/L2). Violates AC-02 multi-resource consistency for plan relocate.
findings.summary: plan relocate tears config vs path when config write fails after durable persist
